question: Zeeshan travels 294 km at 42 km/hr, the next 210 km at 30 km/hr and the next 330 km at 66 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey? (Round off your answer to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = 294 + 210 + 330 = 834 km

Total Time = (294 ÷ 42) + (210 ÷ 30) + (330 ÷ 66) = 7 + 7 + 5 = 19 hr

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Average Speed = 834 ÷ 19 ≈ 43.89 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 43.89 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance D₁ = 294 km, Speed S₁ = 42 km/hr

Distance D₂ = 210 km, Speed S₂ = 30 km/hr

Distance D₃ = 330 km, Speed S₃ = 66 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ T₁ = 294 ÷ 42 = 7 hr

⇒ T₂ = 210 ÷ 30 = 7 hr

⇒ T₃ = 330 ÷ 66 = 5 hr

⇒ Total Time = 7 + 7 + 5 = 19 hr

⇒ Total Distance = 294 + 210 + 330 = 834 km

⇒ Average Speed = 834 ÷ 19 = 43.8947... km/hr

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 43.89 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 43.89 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Different Distances)

It is the ratio of the total distance covered to the total time taken. Formula: Avg Speed = (D₁ + D₂ + ...) ÷ (T₁ + T₂ + ...)

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a person covers two equal halves of a journey at speeds x and y, the average speed is (2xy) ÷ (x + y). For three equal parts at speeds x, y, and z, it is (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.
